title: Performance Optimization in Next.js
description: Eliminate query waterfalls, implement parallel data fetching, optimize connection pools, and leverage React cache().

data.text: When building data-intensive applications in Next.js, poorly structured database queries create significant latency. By adopting parallel fetching (`Promise.all`), eliminating sequential waterfalls, and deduplicating queries using React `cache()`, you can drastically reduce page load times.
Pattern 1: Parallel Data Fetching with Promise.all

data.title: Sequential Waterfall vs Parallel Execution

data.text: In React Server Components, multiple components in the component tree (e.g. `Navbar`, `Sidebar`, and `ProfilePage`) often need the same current user profile. Wrapping your Prisma query with React's `cache()` deduplicates the query within a single render pass, executing the SQL query exactly once.

data.title: lib/data/user.ts with React cache()
data.content: Deduplicated query accessible across multiple Server Components.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `Promise.all` to fetch independent datasets in parallel.
Use React `cache()` to deduplicate identical Prisma queries across the component tree.
Always use `select` to minimize database bandwidth and memory consumption.
